clue.text: Politician and pilot more relaxed, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the starting sounds of a pair of words

blocks.note: to pilot is to steer, and more relaxed is calmer; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A politician and an airline pilot compared for who keeps the cooler head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping ST and the hard C of STEER CALMER gives the answer; in British speech CALMER and the surname's second syllable rhyme, as the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer is a British Labour politician who became Prime Minister in 2024.

clue.text: Comfort stop when caught out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for caught is taken away from the word

blocks.note: to stop is to cease
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A comfort break on a journey ends when someone is caught short.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C from CEASE to leave EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of comfort, freedom from pain or worry.

clue.text: Run away in defeat

blocks.note: surface reading: someone flees after losing
setter's reading: a disorderly flight of a beaten army, or a crushing defeat

explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction to flee, but the whole clue describes the noun: a beaten army scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a disorderly retreat of defeated troops, and also an overwhelming victory over them.

clue.text: Article with more complicated proposition

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the definite article
rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece makes a more involved suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition that can be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Group demanding NI reduction somewhat upset

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: found across the end of demanding, NI and the start of reduction

explanation.surface: A lobby group is unhappy at calls to cut National Insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is National Insurance, the UK payroll tax. The letters G-N-I-R straddle three words and are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a group of people working together, often secretly, like a spy ring.

clue.text: All together in Paris?

blocks.note: surface reading: everyone gathered in one place
setter's reading: how the French put it, a phrase borrowed into English

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a group trip to Paris; really it asks for the French phrase for all together, which English also uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French phrase means as a whole group, all at once.

clue.text: Veal cooked with old hen's fat

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are prepared and changed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A recipe of veal and an old hen sounds rich and fatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Love handles is an informal term for deposits of fat at the sides of the waist.

clue.text: Delicate creature, description of Mona Lisa?

blocks.note: first meaning: a common migratory butterfly
second meaning: Leonardo's portrait shows a woman in paint

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the Mona Lisa as a lady who has been painted.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted lady is an orange-and-black butterfly, a fragile insect; and the Mona Lisa is literally a portrait of a woman.

clue.text: Crowd has regularly ignored closing bars

indicators.note: dropping letters at a regular interval leaves every other one

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An audience has stopped listening by the final bars of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Madman uses unusual European alias

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A deranged man adopts a strange European false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false name someone goes by, which is what an assumed name is.

clue.text: Reportedly torch Swiss city

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the answer is spelt differently from the word it sounds like

blocks.note: to torch something is to set it alight

explanation.surface: News reports of arson in a Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bern is the Swiss capital, the seat of the federal government.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, kids coped eating dry pudding

indicators.note: something unexpected breaks the usual order, so these letters are reshuffled
eating takes one thing inside another

blocks.note: rearranged
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Children surprisingly managed to eat a dry pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry means teetotal here, not lacking moisture. Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants, a school-dinner classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a traditional British dessert, the kind of thing the British call a pudding.

clue.text: Deceitful plan from criminal I can convert

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook boasts of a scam to turn things around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like the anagram signal; it is part of the letters, and 'criminal' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrivance is a cunning scheme or trick, an artful device to deceive.

clue.text: Support the new seer

indicators.note: new means made over afresh, so the preceding word's letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: a prop holds something up
rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing the latest visionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet foretells the future, as a seer does.

clue.text: Greek character exercises in shade

blocks.note: tau is the Greek letter T
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A Greek man works out in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey colour, a shade in the paint-chart sense.

clue.text: Set aside ravioli so latecomer eats

indicators.note: the surrounding words swallow the answer whole, so it sits inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of ravioli, the word so and the start of latecomer

explanation.surface: Someone saves ravioli for a guest who arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate something and keep it apart from the rest.

clue.text: Story in film uncovered the first year of Christ's life?

indicators.note: uncovered strips away the outside, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its outer letters
Roman numeral one
Anno Domini, years counted from Christ's birth

explanation.surface: A film about the infant Jesus tells a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The first year of the Christian era is AD 1, written here as I and AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War, a story in verse.

clue.text: Elderly detective right to leave wood

indicators.note: the abbreviation must go away from the name, leaving the rest

blocks.note: Miss Marple, Agatha Christie's elderly amateur sleuth
R is short for right

explanation.surface: An aged sleuth exits correctly into the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a timber, so the tree's wood goes by the same name.

clue.text: Item of clothing couple picked up — and again!
I perform with large star

blocks.note: taken as written
to do is to perform
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A performer brags about appearing with a big name.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a celebrity who is adored, as a star is.

clue.text: Start to scoff fruit and asparagus?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Begin by eating fruit and asparagus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: an asparagus shoot is one particular spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a single shoot of asparagus, from its pointed shape.

clue.text: Spy who's gone off?

blocks.note: first meaning: an agent who lies dormant until activated
second meaning: someone who has gone off to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' suggests turned bad or left; here it means dropped off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a planted agent waiting for orders, and also a person who is asleep.

clue.text: Sally's film turned up after trip to timeless south

indicators.note: timeless means without the abbreviation for time, so that letter is dropped
in a down clue, turned up means flipped upwards, so read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written, then loses its T
taken as written, then loses its T
S is short for south
E.T., Spielberg's alien film

explanation.surface: Sally's film flopped after a journey south.
explanation.walkthrough: Timeless applies to both trip and to, leaving RIP and O. A sally is a witty retort, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty reply, which is what a riposte is.

clue.text: Letter from English student found in skiing area

indicators.note: found in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: E is short for English
a piste is a ski run
L is the learner plate

explanation.surface: A letter home from an English student at a ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or literary letter, like those of the New Testament.

clue.text: Stretch Germany before first goal

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
1st, with the numeral read as the letter I
an end is an aim

explanation.surface: Germany extend their lead before the opening goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or expand by stretching outward.

clue.text: Bore Doctor and Silver

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
joins the two pieces
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A dull GP called Silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is a tedious thing or person, a bore.

clue.text: Faction in debt with nothing to lose

indicators.note: to lose means to drop something, so that letter goes

blocks.note: someone in debt is owing money
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A party faction in debt has nothing more to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a section of a political party with its own views, a faction.

clue.text: Book shows

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the Bible
second meaning: items on a variety bill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book shows' reads as reserve tickets; both words are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts is a New Testament book, and acts are performances or turns on a stage.

clue.text: Home and Foreign Office news cut short

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Domestic and diplomatic departments trimming their bulletins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition itself signals the abbreviation of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a clipped form of information, which is news in brief.

clue.text: Go back in a flash

blocks.note: to split is slang for to leave
to back a motion is to second it

explanation.surface: Return instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' looks like one phrase meaning return; split it into two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an instant, a very brief moment like a flash.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot bird

blocks.note: first meaning: raise a gun's hammer ready to fire
second meaning: a male chicken

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hunter aiming at a bird; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a gun is to set its firing mechanism, and a cock is a male fowl.

clue.text: Sequence of prisoners go free

indicators.note: set free, the letters are released from their order and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A line of inmates walking out of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A progression is a series of things following in order, a sequence.
